That catalogue mix is the Webflow implementation filter — not a generic ecommerce lecture.

Buyer question: for online storefront teams, is Webflow worth the Site Premium unlock, or does Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the list price floor alone kill the rollout?

ROI gate: Webflow is worth the Site Premium spend if online storefront + product catalog are weekly; not worth buying when Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the list price floor alone.

Best for: Design-led brands that want a custom site and a curated catalog on one visual CMS; Teams that outgrew Wix/Squarespace templates but do not need a commerce OS; Founders who will model Site + Ecommerce TCO and stay inside item caps (Design-led brands that want a custom site and a curated catalog on one visual CMS).

Poor fit when: High-SKU catalogs, heavy B2B, or marketplace ops; Retailers whose center of gravity is POS hardware; Teams that want a single all-in-one commerce OS (see Shopify). Avoid if Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the list price floor alone would block go-live.

sections.heading: Webflow limitation, pricing interpretation, and alternative context
sections.body:
Limitation: Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the list price floor alone; Catalog caps (500 / 5,000 / 15,000 items) and Standard’s 2% transaction fee trail Shopify-class commerce OS depth; No native retail POS — Webflow is website-builder commerce, not omnichannel hardware because it forces process changes or add-ons around Webflow when online storefront is the job.

Pricing interpretation: no free plan confirmed — scope a paid pilot on Site Premium with exit criteria before annual seats.

Plan trade-off: you gain dropshipping sourcing (Site Premium, Ecommerce Standard, Ecommerce Plus, Ecommerce Advanced) at the expense of Subscription floors vs payment-processing spreads and GMV/overage fees — measure both in the pilot. Researched packaging: Site Premium · online storefront | Ecommerce Standard | Ecommerce Plus.

Alternative context: unlike Wix, Webflow is preferable when Design-led brands that want a custom site and a curated catalog on one visual CMS because online storefront plus dropshipping sourcing (Site Premium, Ecommerce Standard, Ecommerce Plus, Ecommerce Advanced) match; prefer Wix when High-SKU catalogs, heavy B2B, or marketplace ops because the operating loops differ.

sections.heading: Decision scenario and conclusion for Webflow
sections.body:
Workflow advantage: Webflow is faster for online storefront when online storefront; product catalog; checkout payments; order management is in-product; skip when Ecommerce requires a Site plan in addition to the Ecommerce plan — model combined TCO, not the list price floor alone because that loop lives elsewhere.

Implementation complexity: setup requires confirming dropshipping sourcing (Site Premium, Ecommerce Standard, Ecommerce Plus, Ecommerce Advanced) ownership and Stripe before rollout — do not scale seats first.

Integrations in research: Stripe, PayPal.

Conclusion: Webflow is worth it if Design-led brands that want a custom site and a curated catalog on one visual CMS and dropshipping sourcing (Site Premium, Ecommerce Standard, Ecommerce Plus, Ecommerce Advanced) are weekly; skip Webflow if High-SKU catalogs, heavy B2B, or marketplace ops. That is the decision, not a template with the logo swapped.
